en: With je, the reflexive word is me: je me lève.
With tu, the reflexive word is te: tu te réveilles.
With il or elle, the reflexive word is se: il se lave.
With nous, the reflexive word is also nous: nous nous habillons.
With vous, the reflexive word is also vous: vous vous couchez.
With ils or elles, the reflexive word is se: elles se brossent.
What does je me lève mean?
Se lever means to get up.
What does je me couche mean?
Se coucher means to go to bed.
What does je me douche mean?
Se doucher means to have a shower.
Me becomes m’ before a vowel or a silent h: je m’habille.
Se becomes s’ before a vowel: il s’appelle Lucas means his name is Lucas.
How do you say My name is Emma in French?
With je, use m’ before appelle: je m’appelle.
With nous, the reflexive word is nous, so nous appears twice.
How do you say She brushes her hair in French?
With elle, use se and the verb form brosse.
How do you say We have a wash in French?
We is nous, and the reflexive word with nous is nous.
Which sentence has the right word order?
The reflexive word goes just before the verb: je me brosse.
Le soir, je me ___ à neuf heures.
With je, the verb ends in -e: je me couche.
Tu te ___ les mains avant de manger.
With tu, the verb ends in -es: tu te laves.
Mon père se ___ à six heures.
Mon père is il, so the verb is lève: il se lève.
In the negative, the reflexive word stays before the verb: je ne me lève pas.
Ne comes first, then se and the verb, then pas.
With nous, the reflexive word is nous: nous nous dépêchons.
Se dépêcher means to hurry, for example to catch the bus.
S’endormir means to fall asleep. Se réveiller means to wake up.
With vous, the verb ends in -ez: vous vous réveillez.
Les enfants means they (ils), so the reflexive word is se.
What does je me repose mean?
Se reposer means to rest. It does not mean to reposition.
How do you say I wake up at half past six in French?
Je me réveille à six heures et demie.
Je me réveille à six heures et quart.
Je te réveille à six heures et demie.
Et demie means half past. Je te réveille would mean I wake you up.
Tu t’___ en uniforme pour l’école.
With tu, the verb ends in -es: tu t’habilles.

example.why_en: With je, the reflexive word is me: je me lève.

en.title: My daily routine
en.teach: Reflexive verbs have an extra small word (me, te, se, nous, vous) before the verb. Me, te and se become m’, t’ and s’ before a vowel: Je me lève et je m’habille.
